title: cookie.serialize rejects a valid leading-dot domain
prompt: cookie.serialize(name, val, options) in index.js validates the Domain option strictly, so a domain with a leading dot such as '.example.com' (a form browsers and real sites still use) now throws 'option domain is invalid'. Leading-dot domains and 'localhost' should be accepted, while malformed domains (double dots, trailing dots, spaces, injected attributes) must still be rejected. Please fix it.
